lots.what_it_is: Catalogued as a 1950 XCEL British 240V enamel electric stove (green). Freestanding green and cream vitreous enamel cooker: two coil hotplates and one solid plate, cream drop-down grill or warming compartment with handle above the oven, side-hinged oven door with oval chrome name badge, timer dial and three switch knobs, splayed cabriole legs, cream splashback with wall brackets.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives. 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking for a vintage enamel stove. The three researcher entries were modern Homemaker benchtop ovens and a Euromaid portable oven ($15 to $85 hammer at Gowans), not this item, and were dropped. WebSearch budget was used up, so no Armitage, dealer or interstate comparables could be checked.
lots.working: No surviving same-item SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For reference only (not a bid basis): a $25 hammer at Gowans for a modern benchtop oven would be $30.50 all-in at 22% premium.
lots.confidence_reason: The XCEL name comes from the catalogue title; the oval door badge is four characters but not legible at the 448x600 photo size even after cropping and enlarging. No sold, unsold or asking evidence for the same item. Not tested.
lots.dropped_entries: All three dropped. (1) Gowans HOMEMAKER OVEN WITH TOP HOT PLATES, $25 hammer, 3 bids, listed 2026-09-20: I re-ran the API URL and the figures match, but it is a modern benchtop oven, not a 1950s freestanding enamel range. Different item and different market. (2) Gowans HOMEMAKER OVEN GRILL, $30 hammer, 2 bids, listed 2026-09-06: figures confirmed, same reason. (3) Gowans EUROMAID PORTABLE OVEN WITH HOTPLATES, $85 hammer, 3 bids, listed 2026-02-15: figures confirmed, modern portable, not comparable. The researcher had already called these category guides; under the same-item rule they cannot stay as evidence. Extra Gowans API searches by me (stove, 1950s stove, metters, kooka, electric range, vintage oven, retro oven, enamel, cooker, xcel stove, enamel stove, vintage stove, retro stove) found no past vintage enamel kitchen stove. Only camp and gas stoves turned up. WebSearch refused (budget used up), so Armitage past results, dealer listings and interstate auction houses were not checked.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: oval chrome badge on the oven door (four letters, consistent with XCEL but not readable), small enamel plaque low on the door glass panel (not legible), timer dial plus three ceramic-look knobs on a cream panel, one black knob by the door latch. Photo 2: oven open, enamel liner grimy with rust on the lower edges, two racks present. Photo 3: top compartment flap open, flap has a tear or split in the enamel or metal at the centre of its lower edge, grill area dirty, a loose tray inside. Photo 4: both coil plates present and look complete, solid plate heavily crusted with burnt residue or corrosion, small chips on the green top. Splashback brackets intact. Legs and side panels look sound with general wear.
lots.condition: Used and untested. Oven and grill compartments dirty with surface rust. Solid hotplate heavily crusted. Enamel chips on the cooktop. Damage (tear or dent) to the drop-down flap. Original wiring of about 1950 should be treated as unsafe until checked by an electrician; a stove like this needs a hard-wired 240V circuit, not a plug.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you read the maker's badge and any rating plate (maker, model, voltage, wattage, country)? Has it been tested or powered up, and is the original wiring and flex intact? Do all elements, the timer and the switches work, and are the oven racks and grill tray complete? How bad is the damage to the drop-down flap, and is there any rust-through on the base or back?
lots.score_reason: A complete-looking 1950s enamel stove in a desirable green and cream finish has some appeal to retro kitchen, film prop and shack or glamping buyers, but it is bulky, untested, grimy, has a damaged flap and a crusted plate, and I found no sale evidence at any price. Most likely value is a modest figure in the $30 to $150 range, discounted for no evidence.
